card.name: Linking words before drug exposure details
card.fires_on: Small linking words or modifiers right before a drug name, dose, or study type in clinical-trial and interaction sentences, such as "multiple" before doses, "received" or "at" after "Among patients who", and "oral" before a carcinogenicity study.

modes.label: Before doses in interaction studies
modes.description: The word "multiple" after coadministration with, leading into doses of the drug.
modes.example: for Famciclovir to Affect Other Drugs The steady-state pharmacokinetics of digoxin were not altered by concomitant administration of<< multiple>> doses of famciclovir (

modes.label: Patients who received the drug
modes.description: Verbs and prepositions in "Among patients who received DRUG at the recommended dosage" phrases.
modes.example: Among patients who<< received>> LUNSUMIO at the recommended dosage

modes.label: Study or exposure descriptors
modes.description: A word that introduces a study type or exposure context, such as oral, for, or with.
modes.example: Tumorigenic Potential In an<< oral>> carcinogenicity study, gabapentin

card.plain: It fires on small connecting words that lead into how a drug was given or studied in trial and interaction text.
